items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited within 0.2 mile of the cables in Milford Bay and vessels should not anchor within 2 miles of the cables in Galleons Passage. Tyrrel’s Bay (11°18'N., 60°32'W.) lies between a point located 2.5 miles S of the N extremity of Tobago and another point, 0.8 mile SSE. Its shores are fringed by reefs which extend up to about 0.3 mile seaward in places.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited within 0.5 mile of the platforms. A mud volcano, with a least depth of 1.8m, is located within an area bounded by a circle with a radius of 200m centered on position 10°22.7'N, 60°55.2'W. Mariners are advised to use caution and avoid the area. Numerous submarine pipelines are located between Trinity Hills (10°06.3’N., 61°05.7’W.) and Mayaro Bay and are best seen on the chart.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board at position 10°05.4'N, 61°02.3'W. See Port of Spain (paragraph 1.33) for more details.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all ports and terminals on the W coast of Trinidad within the Gulf of Paria. This includes Chaguaramas Bay, Saint Peter’s Bay, Grier Channel and basin at Port of Spain, the oil jetty at Pointe-a-Pierre, La Brea Pier, Brighton Pier, and Point Fortin Oil Pier. See paragraph 1.33 for further information.

notes.quote: Pilots from Port of Spain will, if required, board vessels outside of the above port areas, including Dragons Mouth, provided prior notice has been sent by radio.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels using the piers or wharves. Pilots are provided by Port of Spain and can be contacted on VHF channels 12 and 16 and board about 1 mile S of Cronstadt Islet. Vessels should send a request for pilotage and an ETA 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory to the quay and berthing is carried out during daylight only. The pilot usually boards about 0.5 mile SW of the pier head.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels berthing and unberthing at Kings Wharf and Sea Lots. Pilotage is not required for vessels berthing and unberthing at the Caricom Wharves. Vessels should send an ETA 48 hours and 24 hours in advance. Pilot boarding positions are as shown in the table titled Pilot Boarding Stations—Port of Spain .

notes.quote: Pilot Boarding Stations—Port of Spain Pilot Statio n Position Grier Station and Basin 10°36.6'N, 61°37.0'W Sea Lots Channel 10°37.7'N, 61°32.0'W Chaguaramas 10°39.0'N, 61°38.5'W

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory except for government vessels and vessels less than 50 gt. Pilots board in position 10°22.6'N, 31°32'W and position 10°22.9'N, 61°31.2'W. Vessels should send an ETA together with a request for pilot 5 days, 4 days, 3 days, 48 hours, 24 hours, and 12 hours prior to arrival. See Port of Spain (paragraph 1.33) for pilot contact information.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Vessels should send their ETA 48 hours, 24 hours, and 12 hours in advance of arrival. Pilots board at the entrance to the Lisas Point approach channel in the following positions: a. 10°22.6'N, 61°31.9'W. b. 10°22.9'N, 61°31.2'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards near 10°19'N, 61°30'W, approximately 1 mile W of the main jetty head. Vessels using the berths embark pilots about 1.4 miles SE of the SPM. Vessels proceeding to the SPM usually embark pilots about 2 miles W. Vessels must keep their engines at standby while at the buoy.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels in the vicinity of Pointe-a-Pierre are requested not to use VHF channels 6 and 10, which are used for transshipment operations. When alongside the berths vessels are to maintain engines and propulsion machinery in standby to leave the berth under full power on short notice and repairs are not permitted that would interfere with this requirement.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Vessels are prohibited from anchoring within 1 mile of the SPM or within 0.3 mile of the pipelines, as indicated on the chart. In addition, vessels are forbidden to cross any of the submarine pipelines lying off Pointe-a-Pierre.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels berthing at La Brea or Brighton. Pilots board at position 10°17'N 61°40'W. See Port of Spain (paragraph 1.33) for pilot contact information.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited in the vicinity of the submarine pipeline, as charted. A spoil ground is located W of and parallel to the approach lane, as best seen on the chart. Oil drilling operations take place within 2.5 miles NE through N to SW of Brighton Pier. Numerous drilling platforms, obstructions, and submarine pipelines may be encountered in this area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board at position 10°13.6'N, 61°42.5'W for the Petrotrin Terminal and position 10°14.3'N, 61°43.8'W for the Atlantic LNG Terminal. See Port of Spain (paragraph 1.33) for contact information. Tugs are available and required for berthing vessels of more than 30,000 dwt at the outer berths.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Changes of 1 hour in the ETA should be reported. The ETA message should contain the following information: 1. Vessel’s name and call sign. 2. SDW. 3.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The oil field has been declared a restricted area, within which navigation is prohibited to all vessels except those connected with oil field operations and small craft. Anchor - ing, trawling, and all seabed operations are prohibited. The N and W limits of the restricted area are marked by lighted buoys.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: In Venezuelan territorial waters, the Ven- ezuelan flag must be continuously displayed at the fore. At night, on request, the vessel’s name must be signaled by light.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots may be obtained from Guiria. Vessels should give 72 hours notice and confirm or amend their ETA 48 hours and 24 hours before arrival. Vessels are berthed by day or night, but normally only at slack water.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for merchant vessels bound for Rio San Juan. Pilots board in the vicinity of the lighted buoy moored 2 miles ESE of Guiria Harbor Entrance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage in the Rio San Juan is compulsory. Pilots can be obtained at Guiria, 3 days advance notice is required. From Punta Carner (10°07'N., 62°57'W.), the Rio San Juan trends in a SW direction and then NW to Caripito, which stands 51 miles above the entrance to the river.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Vessels should send an ETA 72 hours, 48hours, and 24 hours in advance. Pilots are embarked and disembarked at the port of Guiria. Vessels awaiting a pilot should proceed to the Guiria Sea Buoy (10°33'N., 62°15'W.)

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots embark at Guiria and will take vessels upriver as far as Ciudad Bolivar.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: During the passage over the bar and within the river, vessels must maintain a continuous radio watch. Radio stations are situated at the pilot station, Punta Barima, and Puerto Ordaz. These stations provide voice communications along the entire route.

notes.quote: Vessels must report their positions in the river hourly to Puerto Ordaz, from where all traffic is controlled.
Once permission is granted vessels should send their ETA at Lighted Buoy No. 28 to the pilot station.
Once in the New Barima Channel, position reports are due every hour.
Subject to a vessel’s ETA being reported by radio, the pilot will board in the vicinity of Lighted Buoy No. 28, about 5 miles W of Punta Barima.
The ETA should be sent as soon as possible and again 24 hours in advance of arrival at Punta Barima.
Actual arrival at the Approach Buoy should be reported to the pilot stations by voice radio and the position of the vessel reported hourly until the pilot is embarked.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels entering the river must carry only clean ballast. Vessels must display the Venezuelan flag at all times from the time of entry into the approach channel leading into the Rio Orinoco. No vessel is allowed to anchor in the narrow channels of the river or close to a turn. All vessels needing to anchor in the area between Punta Barima and Mile 137, at the junction of the Cano Macareo, can do so; however, vessels must anchor as close as possible to the right hand bank.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: If the dredge then sounds two long and two short blasts, the vessel must not pass the dredge. 5. The dredge signal must be answered by the vessel. 6. If two vessels are approaching the dredge from opposite directions, the dredge will answer the outbound vessel first.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory on the Rio Orinoco from Lighted Buoy 28.0 and is only available in daylight …

notes.quote: Pilots board by helicopter near position 8°55.8'N, 60°11.3'W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Inbound vessels must send ETA to Lt buoy 0.1 24 hours in advance to the Puerto Ordaz Port Captain via the Control Station “YVM”. Outbound vessels must contact “YVM” when departing the berth and every hour until reaching Lt buoy 0.1.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available during daylight hours only within Rio Orinoco from Lighted Buoy 28.0. Pilots board by helicopter near Lighted Buoy 0.1 in position 8°55.8'N, 60°11.3'W. Depths—

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours. Vessels should send their ETA 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance. Pilots board at position 12°08.2'N, 68°17.4'W (for Kralendijk) and position 12°04.8'N, 68°18.4'W (for Zoutsteiger). Kralendijk—Berth Information Berth Length Depth Maximum Vessel Remarks LOA Draft Beam North Pier — 10.0m 299.9m — 37.6m Berthing length of 125m (including dolphins).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels. The pilot boards in position 12°11.9’N., 68°24.3’W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels should contact the pilot on VHF channel 16 when within 30 miles of the terminal. Tugs are compulsory. Two tugs are used for vessels up to 150,000 dwt, three for vessels between 150,000 and 320,000 dwt, and four for vessels over 350,000 dwt.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Tugs are compulsory. Ships must be adequately ballasted to ensure good maneuverability. Ships should contact Fort Nassau Vessel Traffic Control Center on VHF channel 16 or 12 when approaching the terminal.

calls.quote: Ships should contact Fort Nassau Vessel Traffic Control Center on VHF channel 16 or 12 when approaching the terminal.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels 50 gt and over. The pilot boards in position 12°05.5'N, 68°57.0'W. An ETA should be forwarded 48 hours and 24 hours prior to arrival to the harbormaster. Vessels bound for Curacao (unless specifically directed to another bay) should proceed to Willemstad Harbor where they will be contacted by Fort Nassau.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Fort Nassau, the harbor traffic control cen - ter, should be contacted when within range on VHF channels 12 and 16. A 24-hour watch is maintained. Tugs are compulsory for dry cargo vessels more than 228m in length berthing at Willemstad. Tankers up to 244m in length or more require three tugs; those over 16,000 gt and up to 213m in length require two tugs.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: The following signals for the bridge attendant are dis- played at the harbor office: Day Night Meaning Green flag One green light The bridge attendant must close the bridge. Red flag One red light The bridge attendant must keep the bridge open. Willemstad—Conspicuous chimneys close W of harbor entrance The following signals are given from the pontoon bridge at the entrance to Sint Anna Baai: 1.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The aft range marker has been reported (2011) as inconspicuously located midway up a hill. Having cleared these beacons, alter course passing in mid-channel through the pontoon bridge opening. Maintain sufficient headway to overcome any adverse effect of the wind and current. The traffic signals must be strictly observed, because with vessels berthed on both sides of Sint Anna Baai, the fairway is too narrow for large vessels to safely pass each other.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours The pilot boards 1 mile off Lijhoek (12°04'N., 68°52'W.).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards 0.5 mile S of the entrance or in Caracasbaai. The harbor is entered by day only. The vessel must be properly ballasted to ensure safe maneuvering.

notes.quote: To avoid damage to the beaches, vessels are requested to proceed at a moderate speed when within 3 miles of the S coast of Curacao.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and always available. The pilot boards about 0.5 mile W of the Reef Berths.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots are available 24 hours and can be obtained from Oranjestad. A tug can be obtained from Oranjestad and its services are strongly recommended. See Oranjestad Pilotage (paragraph 2.26) for more information. Paarden Baai (Oranjestad) (12°31'N., 70°02'W.)

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels 50 gt and over. Requests for pilots should be made through Curacao Coast Radio Station until within VHF range, giving 48 hours and 24 hours notice of ETA. Oranjestad Port Radio maintains a continuous watch on VHF channels 11 and 16. For pilot boarding locations, see the table titled Oranjestad—Pilot Boarding Locations .

notes.quote: Oranjestad—Pilot Boarding Locations Northwest Entrance 12°31.9'N, 70°04.4'W Southeast Entrance 12°30.0'N, 70°04.0'W Barcadera 12°29.0'N, 70°02.2'W

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board at a prearranged location.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots embark seaward of a line joining Punta de la Ballena and Morro de Puerto Moreno.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilot embarks on arrival or at the anchorage in position 10°52.4'N, 64°04.8'W. An ETA message should be sent 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance. Vessels will maintain their engines on standby at the anchorage.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board at Puerto Sucre. Berthing is carried out before 0900 due to high winds.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours a day. Pilots board in position 10°27.6'N., 64°12.03'W. Pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: A pilot must be embarked at Puerto La Cruz. Vessels are berthed during daylight hours only.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots embark at Puer- to La Cruz, 1 mile offshore, but are available during daylight hours only. An ETA should be sent 48 hours and 24 hours in advance to “Meneven Puerto La Cruz” by VHF. Berthing is carried out during daylight only, but departure can be arranged for any time.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. An ETA should be given 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance to “Corpoven Puerto La Cruz” through Puerto La Guaira coast radio station. Pilots board in a position that is established with the port captain. Vessels must report on VHF channel 16, one hour before berthing or anchoring.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It is reported (2019) all vessels leaving Bahía de Bergantin must use the channel NE of Isla Burro. The current is negligible, but wind strength in the afternoon and evening should be considered. The NE channel is used by vessels with drafts of 9.1m and greater. Such vessels should enter by steering a SSE course to pass midway between the charted aids.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilots and the terminal may be contacted on VHF channels 12 and 16. Pilots prefer docking during daylight hours only. For pilot boarding locations see the table title Puerto Jose —Pilot Boarding Locations .

notes.quote: Puerto Jose—Pilot Boarding Locations 10°09.2'N, 64°50.1'W 10°07.5'N, 64°50.5'W 10°08.8'N, 64°51.5'W

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Contact with the terminal must be established at least 4 hours prior to arrival, confirm - ing the ETA or providing any changes.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and available from 0600 to 2400. Pilots board in position 10°37.2'N, 66°57.8'W; position 10°35.3'N, 67°04.7'W; or position 10°35.1'N, 67°04.9'W for Conjuno Generador Josefa Sanchez Bastidas.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: An ETA must be sent 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours before arrival. Changes of 6 hours in ETA should be promptly reported.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Due to submarine cables, which may best be seen on the chart, anchoring and fishing are prohibited in an area, about 0.5 mile wide, extending 2.5 miles NNE of Punta Mulatos. Numerous fishing boats may be encountered in the ap - proaches to La Guaira. Many are not lighted and only display their lights upon the approach of another vessel.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots board in position 10°40'N, 67°05'W. Vessels should contact the pilot 2 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The Restricted Area is best seen on the chart.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels navigating in waters S of latitude 10°34'N and W of longitude 67°57'W. Pilots operate in daylight hours with advance notice required for operations at night. Pilots board in position 10°30.3'N., 68°01'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board at the anchorage (0.5 to 1.0 mile N or W of the pier centred on position 1 0°31.5′N, 68°08.5′W) and are available 24 hours.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots and clearance must be obtained at Puerto Cabello.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards 1 mile off the pier head.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Vessels bound for this port should await the pilot either at anchor or underway 2 miles N of the lighted buoy moored about 1 mile NW of the lighthouse on Punta Taimataima.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory Pilotage is provided by Amuay Marine (see paragraph 3.4) and is available 24 hours. Pilots board 1.5 miles WNW of the SSW pier head from a power boat.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards in position 11°40.6'N, 70°13.6'W. Vessels should provide an ETA at least 72 hours in advance of arrival. Pilots for vessels bound for Lago de Maracaibo board off Caleta Guaranao.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: One red light—Entry prohibited. 2. One green light—Entry permitted. 3. Two green lights—A vessel is aground, but there is passage inward. 4. Two red lights—A vessel is aground and entry is prohibited.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards in position 12°18.4'N, 71°59.7'W.Vessels should send an ETA 5 days prior to arrival.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Entry to the port is restricted. Permission should be obtained from the port authorities before proceeding to the anchorage, quarantine area, or the piers. Bulk cargo vessels arriving in ballast are restricted to a maximum draft of 9m, as they are swung in the turning basin before being berthed. Arriving vessels must be carrying clean ballast in segregated tanks, with their holds swept clean.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Precautions must be taken when navigating near this restricted area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels. The pilot boards in position 11°18.8'N, 73°23.8'W. Vessels are required to send their ETA 72 hours prior to arrival at the pilot boarding position.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Tugs are compulsory.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels larger than 200 gt. Pilots board in position 11°14.6'N, 74°13.9'W. Pilotage is also provided for Barranquilla, Puerto Prodeco, Pozos Colorados Terminal, and Rio Magdalena. Vessels should send their ETA and request for pilot 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and Pozos Colorados is a port of entry. Vessels should provide an ETA at least 24 hours in advance of arrival. Vessels are required to proceed to the anchorage off Santa Marta (1 mile SSW of Isla El Morro) to complete free pratique and other operation procedures. Pilots board in position 11°11.1'N, 74°15.0'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position 11°14.6'N, 74°13.9'W and position 11°11.1'N, 74°15.0'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position 11°14.6'N, 74°13.9'W and position 11°11.1'N, 74°15.0'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 200 gross tons. An ETA should be sent 48 and 24 hours in advance. The pilot boards at position: 11°07'N, 74°52.5'W. If the pilot is unable to board because of heavy swell, the pilot vessel will lead the vessel into the river.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Several submarine exercise areas, which may best be seen on the charts, lie 13 miles WNW and 18 miles W of the summit of Isla Tierra Bomba, just N of the S entrance point of Bahia de Cartagena. As these areas are reserved for the Colombian Navy, vessels are requested to navigate with care and keep a good lookout in this vicinity.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels and is available 24 hours. The ETA must be submitted via the ship’s agent 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival. The pilot boards in position 10°18.9'N, 75°35.9'W. Vessels entering Mamonal require a mooring master who will board in position 10°19’N, 75°35’W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels transporting hydrocarbons or other dangerous cargoes are prohibited from transiting. Ships, barges, fishing vessels, and major coastal craft are forbidden to sail through the channels between Isla Arena, Punta Baru, and Isla Grande.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. A docking master boards vessels from a tug/pilot boat and leaves the dock on sighting the vessel. The pilot boards in position 9°32.5'N, 75°50.0'W (tanker anchorage) and position 9°32.7'N, 75°45.9'W (vessels berthing on arrival). The pilots can be contacted on channels 16, 20, and 84; VHF channel 16 is monitored 24 hours.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: A compulsory arrival safety inspection will be conducted by the cargo loading master. Vessels should establish contact with Covenas Port Control when within 30 miles. All vessels loading at Covenas Terminal must send a no- tification 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage and all other bottom activity is prohibited in the area spanning Punta Bolivar and Punta de Piedras, extending in a NW direction for a distance of about 10 miles from the pier head. Submarine pipelines have been laid in this area for the purpose of cargo transfer. Reference should be made to the chart.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is as previously described in the section covering Covenas Pilotage.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels are warned that they risk prosecu- tion if they anchor, travel, or carry out other activities affect - ing the sea bed within the restricted areas. Such areas, which may best be seen on the chart, are situated in the vicinity of submarine pipelines.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 200 gt. Departing vessels should advise the pilots at least 2 hours before departure time. The pilot boards in the pilot boarding area centered on position 8°03.7'N, 76°45.9'W. ETA should be sent via agents 24 hours prior to arrival, and confirmed 2 hours prior to arrival.

notes.quote: Vessels should establish contact with Turbo Coast Guard on VHF channel 16 when 20 nm from the pilot boarding area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards in the vicinity of Approach Lighted Buoy (9°25.7'N., 79°49.6'W.). The pilot may also board near or just inside the breakwater. During rough weather a tug is used for boarding.

notes.quote: Vessels approaching port should advise ETA at least 24 hours prior to arrival.
The pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 10, 12, 14, or 16.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: An IMO-approved TSS has been established in the approaches to Puerto Cristobal. The TSS, best seen on the chart in the outer approaches to Puerto Cristobal, is composed of the traffic separation scheme, several inshore traffic zones, and a precautionary area. Puerto Cristobal (9°21'N., 79°55'W.) World Port Index No. 9860

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for the Panama Canal, including Puerto Cristobal. Pilots board either on arriving inside the breakwaters or at the anchorage. Pilots leave outbound vessels after passing the lighted beacon W of Muelle Cristobal and when the vessel is steadied on its course; however, pilots will accompany vessels to a position just inside the breakwater entrance if desired.

notes.quote: An ETA is required to be sent at least 96 hours in advance.
Vessels approaching the canal from the Atlantic must report 12 hours before arrival at Puerto Cristobal any change of 1 hour or more in their ETA on VHF channel 12.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: All vessels must hoist their designator signals during daylight when approaching and entering Bahia Limon. Vessels must call the signal station on VHF channel 12. Vessels shall, until a pilot boards, maintain a continuous watch on VHF channels 12 and 16. Vessels approaching the Panama Canal shall communicate by radio with the Navigation Division not less than 48 hours in advance of arrival.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Vessels bound S for the Panama Canal or canal anchorages from Colon must first exit Manzanillo Bay through the E breakwater, then proceed to the main entrance to the Panama Canal or anchorages. The Panama Canal

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for mooring/unmooring to an SBM. Pilotage for Canal del Tiger is optional. Vessels requiring a pilot should send a request via VHF. If pilots are not available, vessels should anchor outside the lagoon within 1 mile of position 9°12'N, 82°00'W) Pilots board at position: 8°59'N, 82°05.3'W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels at anchor awaiting their turn at the SBM should maintain a listening watch on VHF channel 16. Vessels anchored within the lagoon should avoid using VHF channel 13 and keep the use of VHF channel 14 to a minimum.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position 9°21.7'N, 82°12'W. Pilots can be contacted on VHF channels 14 and 16. Nancy Shoal (Bajo Solarte) (9°20'N., 82°13'W.), with a least depth of 2.5m, lies about midway between Punta Bastimentos and Hospital Point and extends about 0.5 mile NNW.

notes.quote: A current, which enters Bahia de Almirante through Boca del Drago and emerges through Bocas del Toro, sets SE along the S side of Isla Colon.
A velocity of 1 knot is sometimes encountered.
In the approach to Canal de Bocas del Toro, a SE setting current with a velocity of 1 to 2 knots will be encountered.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for Canal de Bocas del Toro and advisable for Boca del Drago. Pilots are stationed at Bocas del Toro and board about 1.3 miles NNW of Cabo Toro. The pilot should be requested on VHF channel 16 when about 30 miles off. The pilot boat can be contacted on VHF channel 14.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The ETA should be sent through the ship’s agent at least 24 hours prior to arrival. The pilot will board in position 9°59.2'N, 83°00.6'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position: 10°02'N, 83°04.5'W. Pilotage is provided by Puerto Limon.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots boards off the bar.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: No pilots are available and berthing is limited to daylight hours.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots will berth ves- sels only during daylight hours. The pilot boards 1 mile off the port. Vessels should send their ETA 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, and is available during daylight hours only. The pilot boards in position 12°32.2'N, 81°41.1'W in the vicinity of Approach Lighted Buoy.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but pilots are available, if requested, both by day and night, about 0.5 mile offshore.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots are available and board about 2 miles ENE of Punta Oeste Light. The signal for a pilot is one long blast on the whistle or siren in addition to the prescribed flag hoist.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory; reliable pilots are available and should be used. Pilots board vessels about 0.5 to 1 mile seaward of the entrance. The signal for a pilot is one long blast on the whistle or siren.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The entrance must be navigated by eye to avoid the reefs on either side of the entrance and two small coral heads that lie within the harbor, about 0.3 mile from the E shore. A church steeple, in line bearing 020° with a prominent tree, is the leading mark used by local pilots. It was reported that to enter the harbor a vessel should steer 040°, passing about 0.1 mile off a stake on the coral reef on the E side of the entrance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 300 gt. Pilots should be requested at least 24 hours in advance. Vessels should advise ETA directly and to their gent 72 hours, 48 hours, 24 hours, 12 hours, and 6 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 300 gross tons and is provided by Puerto Cortez. The pilot boards in position 15°48.8'N, 87°28.2'W. Vessels should send their ETA 96 hours, 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 300 gt. Vessels should send their ETA 72 hours, 48 hours, 12 hours and 6 hours in advance. For pilot boarding locations see the table titled Puerto Cortes—Pilot Boarding Locations . Puerto Cortes—Pilot Boarding Locations A 15°50.1'N, 87°57.8'W B 15°52.0'N, 87°58.0'W Omoa LPG Terminal 15°49.0'N, 88°02.9'W

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The use of a tug for vessels over 1,000 gt is compulsory.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, for vessels over 100 gross tons. For pilot boarding locations see the table titled Puerto Barrios—Pilot Boarding Locations . Puerto Barrios—Pilot Boarding Locations A 15°56.9'N, 88°39.9'W (on request) B 15°48.5'N, 88'37.0'W C 15°46.3'N, 88°37.1'W

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: When the quarantine flag is hauled down, one short blast must be sounded. Puerto Barrios (aerial view)

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It has been reported (2009) the channel buoys are out of position. Puerto Santo Tomas de Castilla (15°42'N., 88°37'W.) World Port Index No. 9625

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots will board at position 16°21.66'N, 88°24.02'W (Palencia Harbor).

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The least depth in the channel was reported to be 10.1m in 1972, but 7.3m should be considered as a prudent controlling depth. To enter Inner Channel or Main Channel from the S, a vessel’s position should be accurately determined to enable a course to be shaped to clear all the dangers S and W of Sapodilla Cay (16°05'N., 88°17'W.).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The Belize City pilots maintain a station and a lookout on English Cay, about 14 miles SE of the port, Pilots are available 24 hours. Vessels awaiting a pilot should keep clear of the reefs because of the strong set of the current. An ETA should be sent to ship’s agent 24 hours prior to arrival.

notes.quote: Pilots board in position 17°19.5'N, 88°00.0'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels, except Mexican vessels under 500 gt. The pilot boards in position 18°43.8'N, 87°41.2'W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The ETA should be confirmed to Port Control 4 hours and 2 hours prior to arrival on VHF channel 16.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: A mandatory Maritime Traffic Control System serves the Bay of Campeche. The system includes Areas to be Avoided surrounding the marine oil fields and at Cayo Arcas, precautionary areas at track junctions, and specified traffic lanes. These areas are best seen on the chart. Control Centers are located at Cayo Arcas, Dos Bocas, and at four additional platforms, designated IXTOC1, AKAL-C, KU1, and ECO1.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels berthing alongside.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The Marine Traffic Control System is a mandatory system which applies to vessels intending to enter the area bounded by lines joining the following positions: a. 20°30'N, 93°30'W. b. 20°30'N, 91°25'W. c. 18°15'N, 91°25'W. d. 18°15'N, 93°30'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots are summoned from the lighthouse for vessels arriving before 2200. At least 1 hour is required for the pilot launch to go from the town to the anchorage off the canal entrance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots are available from 0800 to 1800 LT, Monday to Saturday, and from 0800 to 1200 LT on Sunday. Pilots board in position 18°39.6'N, 93°10.6'W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Any change of ETA of more than 12 hours should be reported.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Vessels should send an ETA through the agent, 24 hours prior to arrival.

notes.quote: In bad weather pilots board just inside the breakwaters.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boat will meet vessels 0.5 to 3 miles off the breakwater. A vessel should not approach the breakwaters too closely, due to the strong currents which set across the entrance. Pilotage for vessels up to 220m long is available 24 hours.

notes.quote: An ETA should be sent soon after departure from the last port of call but at least 24 hours before arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards off the entrance to Coatzacoalcos. Coatzacoalcos to Puerto Veracruz

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 500 gt, and is available 24 hours. Pilots should be ordered through the agent at least 24 hours in advance and contacted 1 hour prior to arrival on VHF channel 13. The pilot boards in position 19°12.0'N, 96°01.0'W or position 19°15.5'N, 96°08.1'W. Anchoring within the harbor must be done under the supervision of a pilot.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: A Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) has been established in the approaches to Veracruz; vessels should contact Veracruz Traffic when entering the TSS. In normal weather, there are no restrictions on entry or departure, the sole consideration being the draft of the vessel. If the vessel has a draft of more than 8.8m, the tide must be taken into consideration.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 500 gt and should be requested 24 hours in advance through the agent. The pilot boards in position 20°59'50.4''N, 97°15'00.6''W. Vessels should send an ETA at least 48 hours in advance. Movements into and out of the port are restricted to daylight hours.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels, and optional for Mexican vessels under 500 gt. Vessels may anchor there while awaiting the pilot. Pilots board in position 22°16.3'N, 97°44.8'W. Vessels should send their ETA and request for pilots 48 hours prior to arrival or 24 hours if arriving from another Mexican port.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards at position 22°29.5'N, 97°48.4'W. Pilots will establish contact 1 hour prior to arrival on VHF channel 14. If communication is not established, vessels should contact the pilots via Tampico Radio.
